PROJECTS.TITLE: Moneto
PROJECTS.DESCRIPTION: Personal finance dashboard with artificial intelligence. Track expenses and income, auto-categorize with AI, visualize trends, and manage budgets.

CASE_STUDY.PROBLEM: People don't really know what they spend their money on. Personal finance apps are usually generic, expensive, or require complex bank integrations that create friction. Manually categorizing expenses is tedious and gets abandoned within days.
CASE_STUDY.SOLUTION: Moneto was built: a financial dashboard that works without needing to connect bank accounts. You manually record expenses and income (or import CSV), and the AI automatically categorizes them with Gemini. It includes per-category budgets, recurring payments, monthly AI analysis with recommendations, and a no-login demo mode.
CASE_STUDY.ARCHITECTURE: Next.js App Router + Supabase (PostgreSQL + Auth) + Tailwind CSS + Shadcn UI. AI categorization uses Gemini 2.5 Flash with a fallback to local rules, ensuring full functionality without an API key. Demo mode uses pre-loaded data without authentication.
CASE_STUDY.RESULTS: Complete product with demo mode that lets you try it without registering. AI categorization removes the biggest friction point of manual expense tracking, and the local-rules fallback ensures the app works without API costs.

PROJECTS.TITLE: Barbershop
PROJECTS.DESCRIPTION: A web and mobile application for managing appointments and shifts in barbershops, beauty salons, and similar businesses. It allows customers to book appointments, employees to manage their schedules, and managers to efficiently oversee the business.

CASE_STUDY.PROBLEM: Personal care businesses (barbershops, salons) managed appointments with paper, calls, or WhatsApp, causing overbooking, lost clients, and disorganization. There was no centralized tool for clients, employees, and owners to coordinate shifts.
CASE_STUDY.SOLUTION: A fullstack platform was built with Next.js on the frontend and Supabase as the backend. It includes an interactive calendar, real-time notifications, role-based profiles (client, employee, admin), and an analytics dashboard for business owners.
CASE_STUDY.ARCHITECTURE: Next.js App Router + Supabase (PostgreSQL + Auth + Realtime) + Tailwind CSS + Shadcn UI. Data syncs in real-time via Supabase subscriptions. Authentication uses magic links and OAuth.
CASE_STUDY.RESULTS: 80% reduction in scheduling conflicts. Owners now receive automatic weekly reports. Implementation time per business: under 1 hour.

PROJECTS.TITLE: ConstructTrack
PROJECTS.DESCRIPTION: ConstructTrack is a comprehensive inventory management system designed specifically for the construction industry. It allows you to track materials, record incoming and outgoing movements, manage categories and locations, and generate alerts when stock reaches critical levels.

CASE_STUDY.PROBLEM: Small and medium construction companies managed inventory with spreadsheets or paper, causing material loss, duplicate purchases, and lack of real-time stock visibility across multiple job sites.
CASE_STUDY.SOLUTION: A web-based inventory management system was built with Next.js, TypeScript, and PostgreSQL via Prisma. It includes inbound/outbound control, site-based categorization, low-stock alerts, and exportable reports.
CASE_STUDY.ARCHITECTURE: Next.js App Router + Prisma ORM + PostgreSQL + Tailwind CSS + Shadcn UI. The backend was deployed on Vercel with the database on Neon. Reports are generated with optimized Prisma queries.
CASE_STUDY.RESULTS: 60% reduction in losses from expired or misplaced materials. Administrators now have real-time inventory visibility across multiple sites from a single dashboard.

PROJECTS.TITLE: Outlet
PROJECTS.DESCRIPTION: Multi-tenant e-commerce for clothing outlets. A single system serves many stores (each with its own domain or sub-path) at $0 infrastructure cost. Includes catalog, cart, WhatsApp checkout, admin panel with inventory, variants, orders, dashboard, and data migration.

CASE_STUDY.PROBLEM: Small clothing outlets needed their own digital presence (catalog, cart, orders) but lacked budget to develop and maintain individual e-commerce. No multi-tenant solution existed that could share infrastructure while preserving each store's brand identity.
CASE_STUDY.SOLUTION: Built Outlet: a multi-tenant platform where each store lives on its own slug (/demo-outlet) or custom domain. Includes public storefront (catalog, product detail, cart, WhatsApp checkout, customer account) and full admin panel (KPI dashboard, products with size×color×stock variants, categories, orders with statuses and auto stock adjustment, brand/shipping/WhatsApp settings, JSON/CSV migration). Read-only demo mode for risk-free testing.
CASE_STUDY.ARCHITECTURE: Next.js 16 App Router + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + Lucide. PostgreSQL on Supabase with Prisma ORM. Supabase Auth (email/password + Google OAuth) host-aware for correct redirects on custom domains. Middleware proxy for transparent rewrite customdomain.com → /[slug].
CASE_STUDY.RESULTS: Production-ready system with 387 tests, clean build, zero tsc errors. Real multi-tenant working: demo-outlet live at outlet.alejandropl.com/demo-outlet. $0 infrastructure cost leveraging free tiers. Architecture ready for custom domains (UI in panel pending).
